events.name: TouchDesigner ESP32s and Sensors!
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/touchdesigner-esp32s-and-sensors-tickets-2004801732951

Wire a motion sensor to an ESP32 and stream the live data into TouchDesigner over OSC and MQTT. No Arduino experience needed!You'll wire a MPU6050 accelerator and gyroscope to an ESP32, flash a starter sketch, and watch the live numbers land in TouchDesigner in real time over OSC, MQTT, or HTTP.
Once the numbers are flowing, the creative side opens up. Tilt the board to spin a particle system, wave your hand scale geometry, or push the temperature reading into a color ramp. The MPU6050 reports seven values, three for acceleration, three for rotation, and one for temperature, and any of them can drive geometry, color, audio, or timing.
You leave with the code and the wiring guide, which is everything you need to rebuild it.

What you'll do:
- Wire an MPU6050 to an ESP32 on the I2C bus.
- Flash the template and join it to the network.
- Send live accelerometer, gyroscope, and temperature readings into TouchDesigner three ways: OSC, MQTT, and HTTP.
- Drive visuals with real motion through CHOPs.
- Toggle each protocol from the dashboard and watch the setting stick across a reboot.

What you will learn:
- How to setup a working ESP32 sensor node with the code.
- How to use the template repository and wiring guide.
- How to get data into TouchDesigner to control your visuals.

Who it's for:
TouchDesigner users who want physical input. The workshop assume no Arduino experience.
Requirements: Participants should bring a laptop with TouchDesigner and Arduino installed.

Instructor :Bio
Woody Poulard (aka GRNCH) is a Brooklyn-based artist/musician whose work focuses on generative audio-reactive visual installations and performances. He uses creative coding applications like TouchDesigner to generate real-time visuals, Blender for 3D design, and Ableton for music production. Trained in both audio and mechanical engineering, Woody also makes physical sculptures using digital fabrication techniques like 3D printing, laser cutting, and CNC routing. GRNCH’s visuals use elements of abstract, futuristic, and hypnotic scenery, often paired with his signature sound: dark, cinematic, suspenseful techno and broken beat.
No masks required
As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ and governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at www.nycresistor.com/participate/.

Monthly Amateur Radio club meeting of NYCResistorRadio curious? Join the NYC Resistor Ham Radio Club (call sign N2YCR) for our open and regular meetings, the 4th Wednesday of each month from 8:00 – 9:30 pm at NYC Resistor (87 3rd Avenue, 4th Floor).
The amateur radio hobby has something for everyone, from Morse code to modern digital modes. Bring projects you're working on, gear to fix, problems that puzzle you, outings you'd like to organize, or just yourself to meet & greet your friendly local hams. Drop by the #n2ycr channel in Discord any time to say hi.
You do not need to be a member of Resistor to be a member of the club, nor do you need to be a licensed amateur radio operator (though of course we hope you'll become licensed with our help).
We aim to create an inclusive, encouraging, and diverse environment to bring together Brooklyn's radio hackers, antenna experimenters, shortwave listeners, toroid winders, satellite chasers, and balloon launchers.
Come make some noise in the weird and wonderful medium of radio!This is a masks optional event.

events.name: Mask Chains 101 -
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mask-chains-101--tickets-2004486179121

You will learn the basics of wire wrapping your own mask chain and go home with your own wire wrapped flower mask chain.In this mask chain class, you will learn the basics of wire wrapping your own mask chain. We will cover tools, measurements, techniques, and bead choices. You will go home with your own wire wrapped flower mask chain.
Your instructor:Hi, my name is Shine, and I am a NYC-based queer artist and educator with ME/CFS. I am COVID-cautious because I believe that pandemics are a tool of the empire and our health is a gift that should be fiercely protected. I create handmade, creative, and multipurpose mask chains and wire-wrapped jewelry using thrifted, second-hand, and vintage materials. My art gives new life to forgotten beads and chains. I believe that looking hot in a mask is praxis, and I hope that my chains help you feel confident in your mask and inspire you to start conversations about masking with the people around you.This is a masks required workshop.
This is also a class where No One Is Turned Away For Lack Of Funds (aka NOTAFLOF). Please use this ticket code at checkout if you are unable to particpate at full price:
NOTAFLOF2026 - This code will give you a both a pay-what-you-can and a no-cost ticket option.
We are a proactively inclusive space, and prioritize creating opportunities for the whole community to engage with our events, across all identities of race, creed, ethnicity, age, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, physical appearance, and ability; please read our Code of Conduct to familiarize yourself with our community's values before attending. We are also an 18+ space, and accessibility information can be found here.
